records.region: Seward Peninsula, Alaska; Boston Creek, McCarthy Marsh, Fish River and Golovnin Lagoon
records.material_pending_reason: FID2572 parts15–17 leave the mapped eastward Boston Creek belt across McCarthy Marsh toward a separate Pargon feeder. Original topography and imagery do not establish this direct interbranch transfer. Downstream Fish River, the lower delta and actual Golovnin Lagoon receiving setting are supported separately.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Fish River is directly supported for the downstream receiving river and lower delta. It is not assigned as completed representative identity of the whole selected system while the Boston-to-Pargon-side marsh transfer remains unestablished. Boston Creek, Pargon River, delta-branch names and Golovnin Lagoon retain separate bounded identities.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass finished. Ordinary correspondence is complete for the chosen upper opening, Boston valley, downstream Fish valley, fragment/stage join, lower branching delta and actual lagoon receiving setting. A single interbranch marsh through-link remains materially unsupported; therefore the whole feature remains source-material-pending, not completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Fish River is directly supported for the downstream receiving river and lower delta. It is not assigned as completed representative identity of the whole selected system while the Boston-to-Pargon-side marsh transfer remains unestablished. Boston Creek, Pargon River, delta-branch names and Golovnin Lagoon retain separate bounded identities.

scope_limits: One specific Boston Creek-to-Pargon feeder/marsh through-link remains unestablished; the missing link is not replaced by common basin membership, nearby names or modeled connectivity.
The chosen opening is supported on an unnamed feeder into Boston Creek; an ultimate natural source or exact scalar name-start is not assigned.
McCarthy Marsh ponds and nearby lakes are not silently treated as one through-lake channel or as river-name aliases.
The connected lower delta includes distinct Fish, Klokerblok and Mudyutok branches. No precise active distributary, tidal-flow state, bank or present shoreline is asserted.
The original source endpoint and rendered endpoint are different positions within the delta approach; Golovnin Lagoon is independently identified as the actual receiving waterbody.
No selected reservoir, glacier crossing, artificial canal or managed transfer was identified in the inspected corridor. This is not an exhaustive basin-infrastructure inventory.
Registry spelling/aliases and Korean names remain unverified; no product application has occurred.

records.region: Northeastern Pará, Santa Maria do Pará / Igarapé-Açu / Nova Timboteua through Santarém Novo to Maracanã inner estuary
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the continuously corresponding selected Maracanã river system, including its bounded eastern Peixe Boi tributary and inner estuarine ending. No name is imposed on every feeder, island, lateral channel or bay.
records.completion_scope: Four independent municipal originals and three complete imagery views support the selected Rio Maracanã system from its southwestern opening through the Nova Timboteua/Porto Seguro joining corridor and Santarém Novo lower river to the inner estuarine bend beside Maracanã town. The eastern selected tributary is directly labelled Rio Peixe Boi. The actual mainstem endpoint is inside the estuarine receiving setting, not the open Atlantic coast.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the continuously corresponding selected Maracanã river system, including its bounded eastern Peixe Boi tributary and inner estuarine ending. No name is imposed on every feeder, island, lateral channel or bay.

scope_limits: The initial stored opening is not a determination of the natural spring or formal headwater naming boundary.
Municipal maps are generalized historical/statistical compilations, and image mosaic dates/current hydraulic conditions are not established.
Meander cuts and the final display segment are matched at ordinary receiving-corridor scale; no exact bank or individual tidal-thread assignment is made.
A named river representative is not a scalar name for the separate Peixe Boi tributary, mangrove islands, adjoining bay or ocean.
Formal name-registry status remains unverified.

records.completion_scope: Parts1–29 and their ordinary corridor joins are covered by overlapping imagery and field-study mapping. Nannimeer lies outside the selected opening; the thesis warns its historical connection is not a simple continuous Nanni course. Bigi Pan and the separate Corantijn Canal are not substituted for selected features. No selected lagoon or reservoir crossing is asserted.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
